comments.text:
During the trade war with China, a lot of American farmers got hammered because China retaliated with tariffs on U.S. soybeans, pork, and other agricultural exports. Farm bankruptcies and uncertainty went up in some regions, especially for soybean growers. The federal government responded with tens of billions in aid payments to offset losses.

On the flip side, many farmers supported Trump because of deregulation, tax policies, energy policies, and frustration with previous trade arrangements. Some believed the short-term pain was worth trying to pressure China on trade.

So the reality is less “all farmers are thriving” or “all farmers are crushed” and more:

export-heavy farms often felt the trade war pain hardest,
some sectors recovered later,
others still struggled with costs, debt, weather, fuel, and global prices that have nothing to do with one president alone.

It’s one of those issues where both sides cherry-pick whichever farmers fit their narrative.
